messages:
sara: heads-up — noticed a perf regression in production yesterday after the kernel-selector change. Token-level p95 increased ~12% on a handful of high-traffic routes. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/kvcache-explore (shrug emoji)
aj: ouch. which part of the token pipeline regressed? scheduling, kernel exec, or KV lookup?
sara: digging in now. profiler traces show extra time in `kv.lookup` and more frequent `kv.eviction` spikes. baseline before kernel change had much steadier prefix-cache reuse.
carlos: are the evictions correlated with batch size changes? the new kernel selection added a slight increase in max batch window (we widened time-slicing to boost throughput). could be higher sequence-length variety -> cache fragmentation.
sara: timeline: kernel-selector bump at 2026-03-02T03:10Z, regression visible by 2026-03-02T04:40Z. quick prometheus queries i ran: `sum(rate(kv_cache_evictions_total[5m])) by (route)` and `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))`
jen_ops: can you paste the exact queries? want to pin panels on the runbook dashboard.
sara: sure — adding the snippets here:
```
# per-route evictions per minute
sum(rate(kv_cache_evictions_total[5m])) by (route)

# prefix reuse ratio by route (reuse / lookups)
sum(rate(prefix_cache_reuse_total[5m])) by (route) / sum(rate(prefix_cache_lookups_total[5m])) by (route)

# token-level latency breakdown (scheduling | kv_lookup | kernel_exec)
sum by (route, phase) (rate(token_phase_seconds_sum[5m])) / sum by (route, phase) (rate(token_phase_seconds_count[5m]))
```
aj: nice. we should add a memory footprint panel too: `max(kv_cache_memory_bytes) by (instance)` and `kv_cache_memory_bytes{route=~".*"}` aggregate by route. if memory grows then evictions make sense.
carlos: i instrumented per-route reuse in the PR (see #2987) but it only tags route when the request enters the router. we might be double-counting for routed-to-fallback variants. recommend: tag cache keys with `origin_route` label at insertion time, and expose `prefix_cache_reuse_origin_route` so dashboards can show true reuse by logical route.
sara: agree. for quick mitigation we can tighten batch window back to previous default and rollback kernel-selector flags for the heavy routes. propose: rollout rollback to 1% -> 10% -> 100% once metrics stabilize.
perf-bot: deploy event: rollback flag `kernel_selector_v2` set to 10% at 2026-03-02T05:05Z by jen_ops
jen_ops: will run the rollback canary now. can someone create a dashboard checklist? need panels: 1) kv_cache.hit_rate by origin_route (line) 2) kv_cache.evictions per min (stacked by route) 3) kv_cache.memory_bytes (heatmap) 4) prefix_cache.reuse_ratio (top 20 routes) 5) token_latency.phase breakdown (p50/p95) 6) correlated kernel selection variant (tag)
sara: i'll open a quick PR to add the origin_route label and a new scrape for `kv_cache_memory_bytes` aggregation. assigning to @carlos to review. PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3120
carlos: on it. also adding a Prometheus recording rule to precompute `route_kv_evictions_per_min` to keep dashboards cheap. sample rule: `- record: route:kv_evictions_per_min:rate5m
  expr: sum(rate(kv_cache_evictions_total[5m])) by (route)`
aj: we should also export a `prefix_cache_fragmentation_ratio` (unreferenced_prefix_bytes / total_prefix_bytes) so ops can see when evictions are wasteful.
sara: excellent — next steps: 1) rollback canary (jen) 2) PR for origin_route label (sara/carlos) 3) add recording rules + dashboard panels (aj) 4) 24h watch & postmortem if p95 doesn't return to baseline (everyone)
jen_ops: rollback canary in, monitoring graphs look like they're trending back to baseline after 25m. will keep an eye. :thumbsup:
sara: thanks — i'll capture traces for any remaining slow requests and dump top keys that got evicted for the last hour.
perf-bot: alert resolved: kv-cache-eviction-spike (was firing 32m)
aj: once stable let's add a long-running heatmap: `sum by (route, bucket) (rate(prefix_cache_reuse_seconds_bucket[1h]))` to visualize reuse vs time-of-day. helps capacity planning.
carlos: noted. i'll schedule a short sync tomorrow to review dashboard visuals and make sure panels are per-route, not per-instance only.
sara: thanks team. saved links: dashboard draft https://grafana.redwood.company/d-solo/kvcache-new/route-reuse, PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3120, ticket INF-4593
jen_ops: adding INF-4593 to oncall board and tagging infra for memory sampling if needed.
